title: a far seal run takes its own sealed replies
intention: A seal run on a box whose bus home is far takes codemother's sealed replies through the tester's shim and receipts them, so none stands undelivered to the tester.
why: Measured 2026-11-13 on akienasus: CAIRN_BUS_HOME=akiendelllinux.local:7419, so reach holds nothing (ticket bc0bbfd33a71) and codemother's sealed reply to every seal this box announced stood on the Dell's bus; 64 stood after one reseal, and test_the_tester_takes_its_reply tooth 5 sealed red on it.
traces_to: Law 6 (open-9d1bb9b4d708: all mail generated by tester is managed by the tester's shim); Law 7 (a refused seal is printed at the exchange); outline 5.5.3.8.
how: D1: in _announce_seals, after the posts and flush, when remote_address() is set, hand each envelope from undelivered(to='tester') carrying reply_to to TesterShim(bus=bus).deliver and record_delivery(id, to='tester', by='tester'), then flush. D2: a red-first proof simulates the far home with patched reach and remote_address.

clauses.claim: with codemother wired, the tester wired nowhere and the home far, _announce_seals leaves undelivered(to='tester') empty and the reply's receipt is by tester
the reply's refused line is printed at the exchange
sealed replies standing before the run are taken too, and a non-reply envelope to tester stays undelivered

decisions.text: D1: _announce_seals takes the tester's replies on a far home, gated on remote_address() is not None (imported from cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py, which is not changed).
D2: the proof reuses the StubCodemother pattern of test_the_tester_takes_its_reply.py over a scratch bus, one tooth per clause.
